In the wake of everything that's happened recently - and due to the traction is has developed - I remembered an old Athenian power-mitigator. What if we implement of a system similar to the Athenian process of Ostracism?

The Athenians used a democratic re-normalisation system in which they could exile an influential politician for ten years on the grounds that they were becoming too powerful, popular, dangerous, ineffective or tyrannical. After ten years they would be reinstated with all their previous property, belongings and positions of influence - but the political landscape would have changed - thus they were unable to have any major degree of control over matters which directly concerned them. For example - after a major war, the exceptional and well-loved general Themistocles had huge influence both officially and symbolically of a huge portion of the Athenian army, rendering him capable of creating a police state. He was ostracised and when he finally returned, a few more, younger generals had proven themselves and the army was now fractured - forcing him to fight large splinters of the Athenian army should he decide to instigate revolution - a demoralising and ultimately futile exercise.

Because of the nature of politics, the ten-year span was necessary to prevent influential people from biasing or abusing the public at the height of their power. I propose one or two-week long ostracisms of moderators based on a continuous round-the-clock subverse-wide voting pool that goes something like this:

  • First we reverse the process of law. The community decides once-per-week whether it wants to enter ostracism-mode, then over the course of the week decides who to ostracise. First we decide whether we want to 'convict', then we decide who. In the little box to the right of each subverse is a simple switch or toggleable box switching between 'I want to hold an ostracism' and 'I don't want to hold an ostracism'. As soon as a majority of subscribers (and just subscribers mind you, no other limitations on this), then the subverse enters ostracism mode.

  • During 'ostracism mode', each subscriber with a certain minimum amount of CCP or SCP on that specific subverse gets to vote (to mitigate flamewars and floods of subscribers from other subverses taking over an ostracism) for as MANY candidate mods as they want. AS SOON AS any Moderator reaches 30% or more of the total vote-capable subscriber count of the subverse, they are ostracised for a week, at 50%, two weeks. This is to ensure that even a relative vocal minority has a chance to speak out during the brief week when the mod they decided to ostracise is removed.The subverse drops out of 'ostracism mode' for a minimum of three days.

  • Ostracised mods are banned from the subverse for six hours. Unable to post for a single day and are treated as regular users for the rest of the ostracism length - unable to moderate the flow of information.

  • If more than 50% of the mods of a community are ostracised during any given period, then the entire subverse is put on private for six hours to let everyone cool down. Then all mods are put on the one-week ostracism with the lowest voted-for third of mods reinstated fully and immediately but without immunity from subsequent ostracisms.

  • Ostracised mods cannot be ostracised two ostracisms in a row and are automatically reinstated after the ostracism period is up, it is not meant to be a permanent solution - but a power-mitigator.

  • I'm probably missing some important bits of info/data weighting here so please comment with any improvements to the system.

This allows subverse communities to control the people who control the information. By tactically ostracising mods during periods where that specific mod is under scrutiny or fire, we can ensure two things - first that the mod involved cannot ban users or delete threads relating to them during that week or two - this ensures that any opinion shifting is done WITHOUT the mod being capable of biasing anything and protects censorship at times when it needs the most protection. It also protects the mod by removing them from blame, if censorship occurs during the ostracism of a mod then it's obvious that it is not that specific mods' fault directly. It also allows the mod to directly interact with the community without the burden of a position of power - this could help ground mods better in their community but idk thats more psychological then political.

So... to be honest with you, modern Chinese media kind of sucks. We're spoiled on good media as english speaking Westerners. I've lived there for a short time and studied the language for quite awhile. It's still worth it to learn.

The biggest problem is that mainland Chinese media is censored to an absurd extent. Chinese literature has some really good books

There are some independent movies that I like, and some kung fu classics, both old and modern. I can recommend some good movies, what do you like?

There are some... watchable..? TV shows, but I suspect that if you want to find anything of quality you'll have to look at Taiwanese media. Mostly what I saw was a lot of animated shows for kids, usually cheap 3D animation. There was a hilariously bad Pokemon/digimon knockoff that was pretty amusing.

The other big category in TV and movies are WWII or anti-Japanese films. Usually the plot involves a small group of Chinese people fighting against the Japanese invaders, and through bravery, luck and clever thinking, they slaughter the invaders and dance on their bodies. It's geared towards reminding the Chinese people how terrible the occupation was and catering to a desire for revenge.

edit: cleaned up my reply

I'm really, really into the animated version of "A Chinese Ghost Story." I like urban fantasy, metaphysical stuff, sci-fi with an emphasis on cyberpunk, and trashy teenage drama comics/books/shows. I like to think my taste is easy and niche at the same time. Political shill movies is, unfortunately, outside of it - I was real into that sort of thing as a teenager but now it just depresses and bores me. Also thank you for such a detailed reply!

I'll do some digging for you, but I hate to tell you that Chinese censors have been banning TV shows because they drift too far from reality, which means that the fantastic and sci-fi are often barely tolerated or not permitted. It's really subjective. There are some shows about time-travel but they're allowed because censors can agree with the overall theme (ie. going back in time to kill Japanese, going back in time to witness and influence historical events from old dynasties, etc.). If I had to guess why other shows are banned for similar concepts, it's because sci-fi and fantasy often drift into dystopian or conspiracy themes. Beijing is basically a couple of flying cars away from being Blade Runner.

If it's sounds like I'm not happy with Chinese media as a whole, you've got the right impression. China can never have the cultural influence that the US or even Japan has with it's strict censorship.

Here are some bright spots: There are some very deep, introspective films that take a look at changing Chinese culture. I recommend trying “Shower”（《洗澡》）or ”American Dreams in China“ (《中国合伙人》literal title is Chinese Partners).

Chinese people love their history, and you'll find many books, shows and movies about famous battles and events. These are usually very good and a great way to get a new perspective on Chinese history. "Farewell My Concubine" is a famous book (also movie) that is highly recommended for it's significance in Chinese film making.

Also try "Hero". Very recommended, but it's also one of the more popular Chinese movies in the west, so you may have heard of it.

If you're into romantic comedies, it's a whole different story. There are a ton of great romantic comedies that I could recommend, and they're often far more watchable and culturally relevant than anything else being released.

The Chinese media complex is pumping out some over-the-top epic "historical" action movies over the last few years.

Red Cliff, The Taking of Tiger Mountain, Assembly
